c.tagline: The bustling capital of Mayotte, a French island department in the Mozambique Channel between Madagascar and the Comoros.

rides: No major international app (Uber/Bolt/Heetch) operates; Taxi Proxi and other licensed radio-taxi dispatch services only

taxi.fare: metered in town; fixed zone fares for taxi brousse (shared taxis)
taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis are metered; shared 'taxi brousse' minivans charge fixed zone-based fares (roughly €1.40 in town by day, €2.10 at night, up to about €6.20 for the longest cross-island routes).

emergency.note: As an overseas French department, Mayotte uses standard French emergency numbers (15 medical/SAMU, 17 police/gendarmerie, 18 fire/pompiers, 112 general EU number) with a functioning hospital system (Centre Hospitalier de Mayotte). That said, Mayotte has faced significant social unrest, water shortages, and elevated crime/gang-related violence in recent years compared to mainland France, particularly around informal settlements; travelers should check current conditions before visiting.

avoid.reason: Avoid the Kaweni shantytown and other informal settlements, especially after dark, due to gang violence and muggings.
Avoid walking anywhere after dark and steer clear of roadblocks or crowds during the island's recurrent strikes and unrest.

hood_desc: The commercial and administrative heart of the island around the Hôtel de Ville and Place du Marché, with banks, ferry access, and most restaurants; the natural base for visitors.
Mayotte's oldest and largest district at the town's north end, now a dense industrial and residential zone with major markets; authentic but not geared toward tourism.
A central residential neighborhood home to the island's main hospital and several administrative offices; convenient and workaday rather than scenic.
A coastal area a couple of kilometers south of downtown with a resort-style lodge and beach access; the closest thing to a resort enclave near Mamoudzou.
A hillside residential district housing the main stadium (Stade Cavani); quieter, mostly local, with sweeping views over the lagoon.

water.note: Supply cuts and contamination risks are common — drink bottled water.

transit.hours: Taxis brousse run roughly 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM, with reduced, higher-fare service until around 11:00 PM; there is no late-night network.
transit.pay: Cash (euros); fixed zone-based fares are paid directly to the driver.
transit.note: Mayotte has no metro or rail system; shared taxis brousse are the main public transport on Grande-Terre, supplemented by 'la barge,' the car/passenger ferry linking Mamoudzou to Dzaoudzi/Petite-Terre and the airport.

air: Dzaoudzi-Pamandzi International Airport (DZA), on Petite-Terre, reached from Mamoudzou via the La Barge car ferry (about a 15-minute crossing)
bus: Taxi brousse (shared bush taxis) across Grande-Terre
ferry: La Barge car/passenger ferry between Mamoudzou and Dzaoudzi/Petite-Terre
Tourist boat trips to Petite-Terre and the lagoon islets

airport.name: Dzaoudzi-Pamandzi International Airport (DZA)
airport.drive: ~15-min ferry crossing plus a short drive

transit.m: La Barge car/passenger ferry to Mamoudzou (about 15 min, frequent)
Taxi from the ferry landing to the city center

tip.r: As in mainland France, tipping is not expected since service is generally included in restaurant prices; rounding up is welcome but optional.
